lines.trans: So our mystery Friday caller was sleeping upstairs under my attic roof all along.
Sorry for the trouble, Mateo. Thank you for guarding this bag all week.
Why could you not simply hand Tomas the wooden train at his front door?
Three years ago, after our grandfather died, Tomas and I argued bitterly over selling the old house.
Family houses and old memories—those arguments cut deep.
We have not spoken since that Sunday. Last week I sent him one short postcard.
Asking him to meet you here on Friday at noon?
Actually, I only wrote: Something from Grandfather is waiting at the Lemon Tree Inn Friday at noon.
Aha! You feared that if you signed your name, stubborn big brother would stay home!
You know older brothers well, Mateo.
Wait—you were planning to hand the clerk the bag and watch from across the street?!
That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Plural los abuelos also means 'grandparents'.

examples.trans: The grandfather is here.

examples.text: Vemos los abuelos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the grandfathers from the door.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for the pedestrian walkway beside a street.

examples.trans: The pavement is here.

examples.text: Vemos las aceras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pavements from the door.

meanings.note: Exclamation of discovery or agreement.

examples.trans: Aha, here were my glasses!
Aha, that explains the noise.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun used in statements and questions.

examples.trans: Do you need anything else from the kitchen?

examples.text: Hay algo dentro de la caja.
examples.trans: There is something inside the box.

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner for distant space or past time (aquella, aquellos, aquellas).

examples.trans: I remember that Sunday very well.
That house over there is a hundred years old.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.
It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Invariable in gender (el hermano cabezota / tres años cabezotas).

examples.trans: It is a stubborn piece.

examples.text: Tres años cabezotas... la verdad, hermanito, yo también te he echado de menos.
examples.trans: Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a cowardly piece.

examples.text: Ese era mi plan cobarde del lunes... antes de conocerlos a todos ustedes.
examples.trans: That was my cowardly Monday plan... before I met all of you.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

conocer.gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet

meanings.en: to know (a person or place); to meet
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg conozco; preterite conocí often means 'met for the first time'.

examples.trans: I know this neighbourhood very well.
Yesterday we met the new neighbour.

meanings.note: Opposite of largo (long).

examples.trans: It is a short piece.

examples.text: Dejó una nota corta pidiendo guardarla hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.
We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Formed from directa + -mente.

examples.text: Sube directamente a la segunda planta.
examples.trans: Go straight up to the second floor.
Ask her directly.

meanings.note: Stronger than English 'discussion'—usually means an argument.

examples.trans: The argument is here.

examples.text: Vemos las discusiones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the arguments from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Rara vez discutimos en el trabajo.
examples.trans: We rarely argue at work.
They argued over an old trifle.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: duele, duelen).

examples.text: Hoy me duele un poco la cabeza.
examples.trans: My head hurts a little today.
Those harsh words cut deep.

meanings.note: El domingo = on Sunday; los domingos = on Sundays.

examples.trans: The Sunday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los domingos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Sundays from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.
Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Present boot forms carry an accent on í (envío, envías, envía).

examples.trans: I am sending a postcard from Valencia.

examples.text: Ayer enviamos la confirmación por correo.
examples.trans: Yesterday we sent the confirmation by post.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a family piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Firmo el recibo en la esquina.
examples.trans: I sign the receipt in the corner.

examples.text: Firmaron el nuevo contrato esta mañana.
examples.trans: They signed the new contract this morning.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.trans: It is a strong piece.

examples.text: ¡Rápido, ciérralo! Vamos a subirlo... esperad, ¿qué es ese golpe metálico tan fuerte?
examples.trans: Quick, close it! Let us take it upstairs... wait, what is that loud metallic bang?

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los hombres.

examples.trans: The man is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the men from the door.

meanings.note: Respire hondo = take a deep breath.

examples.trans: It is a deep piece.

examples.text: Respire hondo, Ernesto. Todavía nadie ha escrito nada.
examples.trans: Take a deep breath, Ernesto. Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el lunes, los lunes.

examples.trans: The Monday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lunes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mondays from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Vaya lío! = What a mess!

examples.trans: The mess is here.

examples.text: Vemos los líos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the messs from the door.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; plural mayores.

examples.trans: It is an older piece.

examples.text: Conoces bien a los hermanos mayores, Mateo.
examples.trans: You know older brothers well, Mateo.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.
We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Describes a mystery caller or note.

examples.trans: It is a mysterious piece.

examples.text: Pues claro que vine. ¿Por qué te escondiste detrás de una nota misteriosa?
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: muere; o -> u in preterite 3rd: murió).

examples.text: Las flores sin agua mueren pronto.
examples.trans: Flowers without water die quickly.

examples.text: Su abuelo murió hace tres inviernos.
examples.trans: His grandfather died three winters ago.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Nombre y apellidos = full name.

examples.trans: The name is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the names from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

pasado.gloss: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)

meanings.en: last; past (la semana pasada = last week)
meanings.note: Agrees with its noun.

examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Bombilla nueva la semana pasada, jabón limpio y mucha agua caliente.
examples.trans: New bulb last week, clean soap, and plenty of hot water.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

pensar.gloss: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)

meanings.en: to think; to plan to (pensar + infinitive)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: pienso).

examples.text: Pienso abrir la cafetería a las ocho.
examples.trans: I plan to open the cafe at eight.
What do you think of this blue paint?

meanings.note: Everyday polite apology or attention-getter.

examples.text: Perdón por llegar cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving five minutes late.
Pardon? Could you repeat the number?

meanings.note: Plural los planes.

examples.trans: The plan is here.

examples.text: Vemos los planes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the plans from the door.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Short for tarjeta postal.

examples.trans: The postcard is here.

examples.text: Vemos las postales desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the postcards from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: En realidad softens a correction ('actually / in fact').

examples.text: La realidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The reality is very important here.
We talk about the reality.

meanings.note: En recepción = at the front desk.

examples.trans: The front desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos las recepciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the front desks from the door.

meanings.note: Viejos recuerdos = old memories.

examples.trans: The memory is here.

examples.text: Vemos los recuerdos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the memorys from the door.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.trans: The week is here.

examples.text: Vemos las semanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the weeks from the door.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.
What is your name?

meanings.note: Sloping exterior roof covered in tiles.

examples.trans: The tiled roof is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tejados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tiled roofs from the door.

temer.gloss: to fear; to be afraid that

meanings.en: to fear; to be afraid that
meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Temo que hoy va a llover toda la tarde.
examples.trans: I fear it is going to rain all afternoon today.

examples.text: Temía despertar a los vecinos de abajo.
examples.trans: He was afraid of waking the downstairs neighbours.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.
Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?
I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person plural verbs (pasen ustedes).

examples.trans: Do you all have a reservation?

examples.text: El patio es para todos ustedes.
examples.trans: The courtyard is for all of you.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: En ese puesto venden flores frescas.
examples.trans: At that stall they sell fresh flowers.

examples.text: Vendieron la casa familiar hace tres años.
examples.trans: They sold the family house three years ago.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.
